html:
SMTO-SCH-0033 — SMTO couldn't accept the resource plan for this step

GUID: b66df7de-fbe4-5079-804f-1788c1707cff
Slug: scheduling-contract-invalid
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: scheduling

What happened

  • Before a step starts, SMTO plans which computer it will use and how much of that computer it may take. That plan didn't match the step, so SMTO rejected it and didn't start the step with it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the conversation and find the step in the Run. Note whether it is still waiting, already running or finished. SMTO only accepts a new plan for a step that is still waiting and has never started.
  2. If you or a tool you use sent a new plan for a waiting step, send it again based on the step's current details, not older ones. SMTO rejects a plan built from older details or one meant for a different kind of step.
  3. If this appeared on its own while a Task was running and you changed nothing, open Technical details in this panel and select Copy error details. In that case SMTO's own record of where the step should run didn't add up, and the exact message shows which check failed.

What success looks like

  • The step shows as waiting or running in the Run, and this error doesn't come back.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the Run or its history, and don't ask SMTO to repeat a step whose result you can't confirm.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Scheduling-profile or user contract validation rejected the request because it does not match the operation binding, execution mode, declared capacity, captured execution target/namespace evidence or the accepted contract revision.

What this means

  • Scheduling-profile/contract validation rejects changed operation binding, target/enrollment namespace, unsupported capacity/access/mode, stale revision, missing/past-admission queue state or an attempt to reshape protected endpoint ownership. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • Scheduling-profile/contract validation rejects changed operation binding, target/enrollment namespace, unsupported capacity/access/mode, stale revision, missing/past-admission queue state or an attempt to reshape protected endpoint ownership.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the current profile digest, unstarted queue state and captured endpoint namespace; a workload assertion cannot create target trust or observation permission.

How to fix it

  • Read the accepted profile with GET /api/agent/resource-scheduling/profiles/<request_id>/<operation_id>, then PUT its /contract endpoint only while the operation is pending and never admitted, sending the current expected_profile_digest, the profile's binding fingerprint and a contract revision higher than the accepted one; observation-mode profiles and multi-endpoint operations (more than one execution target) cannot be re-declared, and a contract that needs an unspecified shared resource scope is rejected. If the error came from enqueue (SchedulingProfileV2 or ExecutionNamespace validation in native/scheduling_profile.py or native/execution_namespace.py) with no contract edit, the captured target evidence is inconsistent: keep the Server log line and report it as a defect rather than replaying the step.
  • Reload the current scheduling profile and submit a compatible contract with the current fingerprint. Observation admission cannot be granted by a workload contract.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported compatible contract preserves the exact operation, accepted execution mode and endpoint/resource ownership before admission.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
